newsitem.title: USA: New Products: Ski and snowboard bags, bug repellents.
newsitem.headline: New Products: Ski and snowboard bags, bug repellents.

text.p: Skiing or snowboarding down the slopes is the easy part. Lugging gear up the mountain is the problem.

SunDog Inc. of Seattle has developed a specialised line of bags specifically designed for skiers and snowboarders, "all designed to protect gear from the harshest winter treatment while giving sports aficionados the ultimate in intelligent toting solutions.
The fall 1997 products include the single ski bag, double ski bag, binding bag, boot bag, and board bag.
All of the bags are made of water-resistant 420d Nailhead and PVC tarp combination fabric, high-density polyethylene and EVA foam.
Prices have not yet been set.
For more information, contact SunDog at 6700 S. Glacier St., Seattle, Wash. 98188. Phone 206-251-8410.

Avon Products Inc. has introduced two new version of its Skin-So-Soft, which has shown to repel bugs without use of the chemical DEET: Skin-So-Soft Bug Guard ($5.95) and Bug Guard Moisturizing Sunblock Spray ($7.95).

The Good Housekeeping Institute reports in the August edition of the magazine that in a comparison of DEET-based repellents with Avon products, the DEET products kept 100 percent of mosquitoes away from a treated petri dish.
Avon Bug Guard products kept away 67 percent.
Original Skin-So-Soft performed as well as the newer Avon products, the institute reported.

At Black & Decker Corp., maker of household appliances, it's Christmas in July. The company has introduced its holiday line of new products. Here's a sample of what will be availble in stores by this fall.

The Flavor Scented Steamer is a food steamer that has a special bowl where spices are added. As the water steams up through the herb or spice, the essences is imparted into the food. The steamer comes in several sizes, ranging from 2 quarts to 4 quarts.
Retail prices range from $29.99 to $39.99.

Black & Decker's Scumbuster SB400 is a cordless, water-immersible appliance that scours and scrubs bathroom fixtures and tiles. The SB400 runs up to 25 minutes on a stick from Black & Decker's rechargeable VersaPack power system. One rechargeable stick is provided.
Suggested retail prices range from $49.99 to $59.99.
For dog walkers who hate to be left in the dark, Black & Decker has developed the LeashLight, a retractable leash with built-in flashlight.
The LeashLight operates on two C batteries and comes with a 16-foot, heavy-duty black leash that is strong enough for dogs that weight between 30 and 80 pounds.
LeashLight will cost about $39.99.
For more information, Black & Decker can be reached at 800-231-9786.
For city kids, there's nothing like a farm. Two new videos for children show the ins and outs of life on a farm and help kids understand where their food comes from.

"Farming for Kids" and "Dairy Farming for Kids" are both by Rainbow Communications, based in Victor, N.Y. The 30-minute videos use the noise and live action of the farm to attract children's attention while Farmer Bill explains about agriculture.
"Farming for Kids" looks at the different phases of a typical growing season, including planting, cultivating and harvesting.

"Dairy Farming for Kids" looks at the different activities that take place on a dairy farm, including feeding the herd, a visit to the veterinarian, seeing a newborn calf, milking and a trip to the cheese plant.
The videos are designed for children ages 2-10. Each costs $19.95. A video plus teacher's guide and handouts costs $49.90.
For more information call 1-800-518-FARM (3276).
First there was Tamagotchi, the latest cyber-pet toy craze. In late July there will be a licensed spinoff, Tamagotchi, The Game, from Cardinal Industries.
The game is an interactive board game based on Bandai Industries' Tamagotchi hand-held cyber pet toy.

In the game, players raise a two-dimensional cyber-pet to full size. The object is to be the first player to raise a fully cared-for cyber pet, or be the only player left with a fully cared-for pet. In this game, the pet never dies.

The game comes with 72 attention cards, which instruct the players on how to care for the pet; four growth meters, which chart the pet's development; four Tamagotchi playing pieces, die and a playing board.
The game will cost about $12. It will be shipped in late July and should be available nationwide in August.
